headline: SEC approves 3x leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETFs as ADA surges 12% on no clear catalyst
summary: The SEC greenlit triple-leveraged ETF products for Bitcoin and Ether — the most aggressive regulated crypto exposure products approved to date — giving the market a structural headline even on a day when price moves were mostly contained. Bitcoin held above $86,000 as traders priced out an October Fed rate hike, and Cardano's ADA stole the show with a 12% jump that analysts attributed to technical rotation rather than any specific news. The rest of the top 15 moved within 3.5% in either direction.

winners.name: Cardano
winners.catalyst: ADA led all gains with a 12% surge in an otherwise range-bound session. No single fundamental catalyst was identified — the move appears technically driven or reflects rotation into large-cap laggards that had underperformed recent rallies.

losers.name: Rain
losers.catalyst: Rain was the session's largest decliner, falling 3.52% with no specific news catalyst identified.

whyItMoved:
Two forces shaped today's session, and they pulled in different directions. On the macro side, Bitcoin's resilience above $86,000 came as traders reduced the probability of a Fed rate hike in October — even with the US dollar climbing to an 18-month high, a level that typically weighs on risk assets. The market read the Fed repricing as a net positive: less tightening risk meant less pressure on crypto valuations, and Bitcoin responded with a 1.43% gain.

The structural headline was the SEC's approval of triple-leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETFs — products that let traders take on three times the daily price movement of each asset through a regulated fund wrapper. These are the most aggressive crypto ETF products the SEC has approved, and their arrival signals a meaningful expansion of what regulated markets will accommodate. Whether retail or institutional flows follow is a separate question, but the approval itself is a landmark.

Cardano's 12% jump stands apart from the rest of the session. No news event explains it — the move appears to reflect technical buying or rotation into a large-cap asset that had lagged the broader market recovery. Hyperliquid (+3.42%) and Dogecoin (+2.80%) also outperformed without obvious catalysts, suggesting some appetite for higher-beta names. Solana slipped 0.64% and Chainlink edged down 0.29%, both within normal noise range. The Fear & Greed index sits at 70 — in greed territory — consistent with a market that is constructive but not euphoric.
worthKnowing: Metaplanet, a Japanese investment firm, sold 10,000 BTC and repurchased 11,000 BTC in Q3 to demonstrate liquidity, ending the quarter with a net addition of 1,000 Bitcoin and total holdings of 44,000 BTC.

OKX and Intercontinental Exchange — the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange — announced a joint venture to launch a regulated venue for trading tokenized US stocks, a significant step toward merging traditional equity markets with crypto infrastructure.
Stripe announced plans to expand stablecoin-backed payment cards to more than 100 countries by year-end, a broad push toward using stablecoins as everyday consumer payment rails.
